patent_grounding.rationale: Reviewed all cited passages against the model. Components, normal engagement, spring bias, overload roll-off, switching-disk freewheeling engagement, separation of drive, and claim-specific pawl restraints are supported by cited patent text. The lone TRANSFER–DISK interface is grounded and expressly limited to freewheeling contact, not continuous torque transfer.

functional_completeness.rationale: The principal torque path and overload/freewheeling sequence are modeled. Axial spring bias and pawl restraint functions are represented in subsystem descriptions and claim-traceable requirements; omission of external shaft context is disclosed and appropriate to the stated internal-coupling scope.

flow_consistency.rationale: Torque is separately modeled as rotational mechanical flow through sleeve-transfer-hub with compatible port directions/types. Transfer-to-disk contact is a distinct mechanical_contact engagement flow, correctly not conflated with torque transmission.

claim_traceability.rationale: Citation map covers model metadata, all subsystems and ports, both retained interfaces, both flows, all four requirements, and each action/step. Claim 1 direction-specific restraints are distinguished from claims 2 and 3 arrangements; citations point to matching claim text.

interfaces.rationale: Revision 5 has one TRANSFER-side record for IF_TRANSFER_DISK_FREEWHEEL, referencing existing TRANSFER_DISK and DISK_TRANSFER ports and ENGAGEMENT flow. There is no mirrored interface under DISK. Sleeve-transfer and transfer-hub connections also appear once each, with compatible port endpoints.

textbook_application.rationale: The model uses physical components as subsystems and function descriptions as functional_basis; sequential behavior remains a causal mechanical description without adding an electronic controller or unsupported state machine. Textbook guidance informs modeling approach only, not invention facts.

summary: Independently reviewed saved revision 5, including its full SJS object, citations, patent passages, and relevant textbook guidance. The duplicated freewheeling contact interface is resolved: exactly one connection remains, with supported endpoint ports and the distinct ENGAGEMENT/mechanical_contact flow explicitly scoped to freewheeling-position contact rather than continuous torque transmission. No unresolved grounding, completeness, flow, claim-traceability, interface, or textbook-application issues identified.
